target.title: feat(read): persist inbound media to workspace staging
target.body:
## Problem

When agents read inbound images (via `media://inbound/` URIs), the image data is available as base64 in the current turn but not persisted to the workspace filesystem. This means if a subsequent turn tries to use tools like `image` (or any tool that relies on workspace filesystem paths), it will fail with "file not found" because the inbound media only exists as an ephemeral payload.

## Solution

Add a best-effort persistence mechanism in `resolveLocalReadPath`:

- When processing `media://inbound/<id>` URIs, writes a workspace copy to `media/inbound/<id><ext>`
- **5MB size guard** (aligned with `STAGED_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES` from `stage-sandbox-media.ts`)
- **Idempotent**: skips if destination already exists with identical size
- **Session cleanup**: `AgentSession.dispose()` calls `cleanupInboundMediaStaging()` which removes tracked staging directories
- **Non-blocking**: staging failures are silently caught and do not interrupt the read flow

## Changes

| File | Lines | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `src/agents/sessions/tools/read.ts` | +87, -3 | Core logic: `persistInboundMediaToWorkspace()` + `cleanupInboundMediaStaging()` |
| `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts` | +3 | Dispose hook: cleanup stale inbound staging dirs |

## Spec Reference

This implementation follows the design discussed for inbound media persistence, matching the pattern established by `stageSandboxMedia()` in `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts`.

## Testing

- **Compile check**: TypeScript `tsc --noEmit` on modified files passes (no new errors)
- **Existing tests**: No regression expected — changes are additive behind try/catch guards
- Future work: L2 (time-based) and L3 (LRU hard cap) cleanup strategies noted as comments
